text: A retrospective is a show that looks back over an artist's whole career. Here a London museum is showing many of Churchill's paintings from across his life.
Poignant describes something that makes you feel a gentle, deep sadness mixed with tenderness. A painting of a happy family feels poignant now because we know a war was coming.
Audacity is the boldness to try something even if it might not turn out well. Churchill says painting needs nerve, not special talent.
A pastime is something you do for fun in your free time, like a hobby. Churchill wrote an essay called Painting as a Pastime.
Pleasurable means giving you enjoyment and good feelings.
Celebrated means famous and admired by many people. Here Picasso is called a celebrated artist.
By profession means as your job. Picasso is saying Churchill is not a painter as a job, but paints well anyway.
To earn a living is to make enough money from your work to pay for your life.
On view means put out where people can come and look, like paintings in a museum.
The Wallace Collection is a museum in London that is showing Churchill's paintings until November 29th.
Pablo Picasso was a famous Spanish artist of the 1900s, known for bold, strange-looking paintings. Even he praised Churchill's art.
Winston Churchill was Britain's prime minister during the second world war. He also loved painting as a hobby.
Dwight Eisenhower was the American president in the 1950s. In 1958 he helped organise an earlier show of Churchill's art.
Franklin Roosevelt was the American president during most of the second world war and a friend to Churchill. Churchill gave him a painting as a gift.
Blenheim Palace is a huge, grand house in England where Churchill's family came from, and where he was born.
Chartwell was Churchill's country house in England, where he painted often.
Normandy is a region on the northern coast of France.
Kent is a county in the southeast corner of England, close to France across the sea.
Gallipoli was a battle campaign in the first world war that went badly for Britain. Churchill was blamed, and he lost his important job.
Revelatory means showing you something new and surprising that you did not know before.
A canvas is the thick cloth that artists paint on. Here it means the paintings themselves.
Ancestral means belonging to your family going back many generations.
To foreshadow is to give a hint of something bad or important that will happen later.
Impending means about to happen soon, often something serious.
Soulful describes something full of deep feeling.
A takeaway is the main idea you remember after seeing or reading something.
Mulling means thinking about something slowly and carefully.
A downfall is a sudden loss of power, success, or a high position.
Professional means connected to your job or career.
To distract someone is to pull their attention away from a worry or task.
Innate means you were born with it, instead of learning it. An innate gift is a natural talent.
To aspire to something is to hope and work toward reaching it.
A masterpiece is a work of art of the very highest quality.
To content yourself with something is to be happy with it even if it is less than you wanted.
A joy ride is a fun trip taken just for the pleasure of it. Churchill means painting can be a cheerful adventure and need not be perfect.
Bricklaying is building walls by stacking bricks with mortar. Churchill did this for fun too.
Diverting means entertaining and able to take your mind off other things.
To reinvigorate is to give fresh energy to something.
Cognitive decline is the slow weakening of thinking and memory that can happen as people get older.
Biologically means in terms of how the body works. Being a year younger biologically means your body acts a bit younger than your birthday says.
A pursuit is an activity you spend time on, like a hobby.
A polemicist is a writer who argues strongly for or against something.
Outspoken means saying what you think boldly, even when others might disagree.
